texts.preamble: Subhash Chandra Choudhary vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 January, 2024 1 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh At Jabalpur Before Hon'Ble Shri Justice Raj Mohan Singh On The 8th Of January, 2024 Misc. Criminal Case No. 19859 Of 2016 Between:- Subhash Chandra Choudhary S/O Shri P.S. Choudhary, Aged About 48 Years, Occupation: Factory Manager And Senior General Manager (Plant Operations), A.C.C. Ltd.
texts.facts: This application coming on for admission this day, the court passed the following: ORDER Vide this common order MCRC No.19859/2016 and MCRC No.1279/2017 are being disposed of. Since common questions of law and facts are invoked, therefore the facts are being culled out from MCRC No.19859/2016. 2. Petitioner Subhash Chandra Choudhary in MCRC No.19859/2016 has preferred this petition under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. for quashing of proceedings in Criminal Complaint No.386 of 2016 pending in the Court of Judicial Magistrate First Class, Vijayraghavgarh, District Katni and for setting aside the order dated 27.7.2016 passed by the Judicial Magistrate First Class Vijayraghavgarh, District Katni, securing his presence through bailable warrant for the alleged contraventions of provisions of Sections 7A(2)(a) and 7A(2)(c) of the Factories Act, 1948 (for brevity "Act, 1948") and Rule 73-E of the Madhya Pradesh Factories Rules. 3. The petitioner is a Factory Manager and Senior General Manager (Plant Operations), ACC Ltd., Kymore Cement Works, Kymore, District Katni. On 30.4.2016 at about 11:00 AM, an activity of clearing a Jam in the Coal Crusher in ACC Plant was being carried out after obtaining all the necessary permits and following the lock-out procedure. After clearing the crusher, the permit was duly returned and restart of the crusher was attempted. During the said process of restarting the crusher, siren was also blown for indicating that the crusher is being started. Deceased Mohd. Hussain, who was an employee of the contractor was given the task of observing the restart process from a safe distance of atleast two meters. Thereafter the deceased shouted and when other persons rushed to the spot, the deceased was found lying down. A crowbar was also found next to him. The deceased was found lying on the floor with an injury on his head, just above the left ear. Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) including the helmet and eye- goggles were found along with the crowbar near the body of the deceased. It was summarized that against the clear instructions and past training, the deceased had tried to insert the crowbar in the inspection window of the crusher and the other end of the crowbar hit the workman on the area between the helmet and the ear. The workman succumbed to his injuries on reaching hospital. 4. The petitioner being Manager and Director of the Plant submitted his personal report on Form No.22 to the Deputy Director of the Industrial Health & Safety, mentioning the accident to be fatal. The injury was probably caused by the crowbar and the same was on the head over the left ear. The Factory Inspector i.e. Deputy Director of the Industrial Health & Safety conducted his inspection after visiting the Plant. As per his report, the deceased was clearing the Jam in the crusher using an Subhash Chandra Choudhary vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/190631712/ 2 iron rod when suddenly the machine started which caused the rod to strike at his head. As per the report, the violation was also found. The Factory Inspector found that the permit was returned before the work had actually completed and it was a case of non-implementation of work permit, thereby violating the provisions of Section 7A(2)(a) of the Act, 1948 in terms of not ensuring proper safety of the workers. The crusher had two small windows, which were left open and the work of cleaning the Jam by inserting the iron rod was done by the deceased. Since the work permit had prematurely been returned and the machine restarted, therefore it amounted to violation of Rule 73-E of the M.P. Factory Rules. The Factory Inspector also observed that there was no proper supervision when the deceased workman was working and therefore, it was an act of violating the provisions of Section 7A(2) (c) of the Act, 1948. 5 . The petitioner was given a show cause notice to which he had replied by submitting the work permit, energy isolation and lock-out permits. The said permits were requested by Rajkumar Mishra and issued by Shubham Tiwari, whose statements were also recorded during the inspection conducted by the Factory Inspector. Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the report of the Factory Inspector is per se illegal. The lock after completion of work was to be opened. The work permit was returned by the deceased worker after completion of work. Window used to remain open.
texts.arguments: For ready reference, Section 7 of the Act, 1948 is hereby reproduced as under:- "[7A. General duties of the occupier.--(1) Every occupier shall ensure, so far as is reasonably practicable, the health, safety and welfare of all workers while they are at work in the factory. (2) Without prejudice to the generality of the provisions of sub-section (1), the matters to which such duty extends, shall include-- (a) the provision and maintenance of plant and systems of work in the factory that are safe and without risks to health; (b) the arrangements in the factory for ensuring safety and absence of risks to health in connection with the use, handling, storage and transport of articles and substances; (c) the provisions of such information, instruction, training and supervision as are necessary to ensure the health and safety of all workers at work; ( d) the maintenance of all places of work in the factory in a condition that is safe and without risks to health and the provision and maintenance of such means of access to, and egress from, such places as are safe and without such risks; (e) the provision, maintenance or monitoring of such working environment in the factory for the workers that is safe, without risks to health and adequate as regards facilities and arrangements for their welfare at work." Learned counsel for the petitioner vehemently submitted that as per the ACC Limited Occupational Health & Safety Standard for isolation and Lockout, the provision has been made in respect of work permit process i.e. para 3.5.2 of the aforesaid Standard for isolation and Lockout, which prescribes the following characteristics:- "3.5.2 Work Permit Process i) Work on the equipment (where multiple isolation is carried out to protect single or multiple workers), is permitted after obtaining a written authorization in the form of a work permit. ii) Permit holder is responsible to initiate and complete the process of isolation and lock out. iii) Permit shall shall be issued in duplicate with colour code as follows: i) Pink- for Permit holder- to be displayed at work site. iv) Follow the 12 steps given in section 3.5.1.2 (Process for group isolation-multiple isolation carried out to protect single or multiple workers) v) Name of all the people working in on the equipment has to be mentioned in the permit at the start of every shift. vi) Permit issuer & isolation officer shall maintain the necessary permit & register records respectively. vii) Isolation officers and permit issuers shall be nominated by director plant/ Unit head.
